description: Pinned tool manifest for the Vibe Coder container image (Issue #4061). Every version the image installs is recorded here; container/Containerfile only restates these values as build ARGs, and worker/deno/tests/container_manifest_test.ts fails the quality gate when the two disagree. `providers` is the catalogue of pinned coding-agent providers and `installedProviders` is the set a default image build actually installs, which the Containerfile restates as the AGENT_PROVIDERS default (Issue #4105).

images.name: docker.io/library/ruby
images.notes: Digest-pinned official Ruby image, itself built on buildpack-deps:trixie, so it ships bash, GNU coreutils (timeout), git 2.47, curl, ca-certificates, ruby 3.4 and python3 3.13 — still no apt install step to rot (Issue #4090). The floors are load-bearing: git < 2.41 keeps a literal --end-of-options in argv (Issue #3714), Psych.safe_load_file (Issue #3661) needs Psych 4, i.e. ruby >= 3.1, and the semgrep virtualenv is built on this interpreter, whose requires-python is >= 3.10 (Issue #650). The base ships no ensurepip, which is why the semgrep toolchain pins pip as its own artefact.

images.name: docker.io/denoland/deno
images.notes: Scratch image containing only the deno binary; copied in via a build stage so no archive extractor is needed.

providers.notes: Coding-agent provider layer (Issue #4067). container/providers/claude.sh reads these pins with jq and verifies the download before installing it; the base Containerfile only selects the fragments via the set-valued AGENT_PROVIDERS build argument (Issue #4105), so a second provider adds a fragment and an entry here.

The second registered coding-agent provider (Issue #4106) — the first addition made purely through the seam. Checksums are of the static musl release archives codex-<target>-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz from tag rust-v<version>, which run on the glibc base image. Pinned but not in installedProviders: a default image stays Claude-only, and `--build-arg AGENT_PROVIDERS="claude,codex"` is what puts both CLIs in one image.

The third registered coding-agent provider (Issue #4107) — Quorum's judge rather than a planner. The checksum is of the published package @google/gemini-cli-<version>.tgz, which declares no dependencies and ships the whole CLI as a JavaScript bundle: one artefact for every architecture, hence a single noarch checksum. That bundle runs on Node, which is why the Node toolchain layer is built before the provider layer. Pinned but not in installedProviders: a default image stays Claude-only, and `--build-arg AGENT_PROVIDERS="claude,codex,gemini"` is what puts all three CLIs in one image.

The fourth registered coding-agent provider (Issue #415, parent #396). DeepSeek serves an Anthropic-compatible API, so it is carried on the *same upstream artefact* as the claude entry — this duplication is deliberate and must not be collapsed into the claude pin. Two things depend on it: the CLI is installed as `deepseek`, because both fragments run in an AGENT_PROVIDERS="claude,deepseek" image and a shared binary name would mean one provider silently overwriting the other; and the version is pinned independently, because DeepSeek's endpoint is a third party tracking Anthropic's API surface and holding `deepseek` on a known-good CLI version while `claude` moves ahead is the point of the second pin. Pinned but not in installedProviders: a default image stays Claude-only, and `--build-arg AGENT_PROVIDERS="claude,deepseek"` is what puts both CLIs in one image.

toolchains.notes: Each of these repos commits its own shellcheck gate (quality/shellcheck.sh or an inline loop) and hard-fails without the binary — previously satisfied by a Homebrew install on the host.
private-repo-22's quality.sh lints its workflows with actionlint. Remove this toolchain if that repo leaves the fleet.

`cargo deny check` is not optional in these gates: private-repo-16 exits non-zero when the binary is absent and private-repo-17 runs it unguarded. The linux release is a static musl build, so it runs on the glibc base image.

The runtime markdownlint-cli2, Playwright and the Gemini CLI provider need; the worker itself is Deno. Node 24 is the current LTS line. Its Containerfile layer sits before the coding-agent provider layer because a provider fragment whose CLI is a JavaScript bundle needs it at install time (Issue #4107). It ships an npm of its own, but the `npm` toolchain below owns that command (Issue #475) — one pin per command, so the version the image carries is never whatever the Node tarball happened to bundle.

Pinned separately from Node (Issue #475): Node 24.19.0 bundles npm 11.17.0, so every build logged a 'New major version of npm available' notice and the image tracked whatever npm the runtime tarball carried. Installed over the bundled copy from a checksum-verified tarball, like the other npm-sourced tools. npm 12 requires node ^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0, which the pinned Node 24.19.0 satisfies — bump the two together. Pure JavaScript, so one noarch checksum covers both architectures.

Drives the check-markdownlint gate stage against .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc; without it the stage SKIPs and structural Markdown breakage reaches merge. Pure JavaScript, so one noarch checksum covers both architectures — the pin matches .github/workflows/markdown-lint.yml so the container and CI report identical findings.

Standalone rust-lang distribution installed into /usr/local, so no rustup and nothing to update at run time. The combined rust-<version> package carries only rustc/cargo/rust-std/rust-docs, so rustfmt and clippy are fetched as their own component packages — hence the rustfmt_/clippy_ checksum keys, one per architecture. 1.98.0 is the channel four fleet repos pin in rust-toolchain.toml: private-repo-22, private-repo-21, private-repo-15, and a fourth consumer confirmed by Issue #309 whose private-repo-N alias is not recorded in this file — see docs/CONTAINER.md for the cleartext list. Bump those repos and this pin together, or a new stable's clippy lints break their -D warnings gates.

Backs the semgrep quality-gate stage (worker/deno/lib/semgrep_check.ts, Issue #559): without the binary that stage reported SKIPPED on every fleet run and agents met SAST findings only in CI (Issue #650). The version is not a free choice — it must equal SEMGREP_IMAGE_TAG in worker/deno/lib/pinned_actions.ts, the semgrep/semgrep image .github/workflows/semgrep.yml runs, so a local pass predicts a CI pass; container_manifest_test.ts fails the gate on drift. Semgrep's CLI is a Python application with no standalone binary release, so the pins are the manylinux wheels, one per architecture — each bundles its own ~260 MB semgrep-core. The `pip` entry under `tools` is the installer that puts them there; Debian's python3 ships no ensurepip, so the installer is an artefact in its own right and is pinned like everything else. The wheel is installed into a /opt/semgrep virtualenv rather than the system interpreter, which PEP 668 marks externally managed. Only semgrep's own dependency wheels come from the index unverified, the same residual risk `playwright-core install --with-deps` carries for its apt set.

tools.name: pip
tools.notes: Build-time only (Issue #650): the installer that puts the pinned semgrep wheel into the /opt/semgrep virtualenv. Debian's python3 ships no ensurepip, so pip is downloaded as its own checksum-verified wheel and run straight from that file as a zipapp — nothing installs pip into the image, and the system interpreter stays PEP 668 externally managed. Pure Python, so one noarch checksum covers both architectures. Bump it with the semgrep toolchain, or on its own when a pip release fixes an installer bug.

tools.name: playwright-core
tools.notes: Installs headless Chromium into browsersPath at build time (Issues #4069, #274), so the worker captures PR evidence with no host browser and no download mid-run. The version is not a free choice: it is exactly what @playwright/mcp@<PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_VERSION> depends on, because Playwright resolves browsers as chromium-<revision> and each release pins its own revision — worker/deno/tests/container_manifest_test.ts fails the gate when this drifts from PLAYWRIGHT_INSTALLER_VERSION in worker/deno/setup/screenshot.ts. The noarch checksum is the npm tarball (pure JavaScript, one digest for both architectures). chromium_amd64 / chromium_arm64 are the browser zips Playwright then fetches — Chrome for Testing 149.0.7827.3 (linux64) and Playwright chromium revision 1224 (linux-arm64) for this pin. The build downloads those zips, verifies the committed digest, extracts them, then runs `playwright-core install --with-deps chromium` so apt still installs the system-library set. Apt packages stay unpinned by design: Playwright's install-deps list is large and Debian security updates move the versions; pinning them would break the next point release and blow the Containerfile size cap. Residual risk: `--with-deps` trusts Debian's signed apt repos on the digest-pinned trixie base rather than a committed per-package SHA-256.
